subject: maths
title: Chapter 3 · Test 1
summary: Fifteen questions on Pythagoras’ theorem in 2D and 3D, the trigonometric ratios, finding sides and angles, and angles of elevation and depression.
body: This test covers Chapter 3: Pythagoras’ theorem (in 2D and 3D), the trigonometric ratios, finding side lengths and angles with trigonometry, and angles of elevation and depression. It has 15 questions, from easy to challenge. Allow about 25 minutes and work with no notes. You need a scientific calculator for this chapter — set it to degree mode before you start. Diagrams are drawn to scale, but always calculate rather than measure. Sketch and label the right-angled triangle for each question, round only at the end, and give the units.

questions.prompt: Find the length of the hypotenuse x.
questions.explanation: x² = 9² + 40² = 1681, so x = 41 cm. Adding the lengths (49) skips the squaring.
steps: x is opposite the right angle, so it is the hypotenuse: x² = 9² + 40².

mistakes.A: Step 2: you added the lengths. Square each side first, then add.
mistakes.C: Step 3: 1681 is x². Take the square root.
mistakes.D: Step 2: to find the hypotenuse, add the squares — don’t subtract them.

questions.diagram_alt: A right-angled triangle with shorter sides 40 cm and 9 cm and hypotenuse x.

questions.prompt: Write cos θ for the triangle shown.
questions.explanation: cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse = 21/29. 20/29 uses the wrong pair of sides.
steps: Label from θ: opposite = 20, adjacent = 21, hypotenuse = 29.

mistakes.A: Step 2: 20/29 is sin θ (SOH). Cos is CAH.
mistakes.B: Step 2: 20/21 is tan θ (TOA). Cos is CAH.
mistakes.C: Step 3: the fraction is upside down. In CAH, the adjacent goes on top.

questions.diagram_alt: A right-angled triangle with 21 cm next to θ, 20 cm across from θ, and hypotenuse 29 cm.

questions.prompt: Find x, the side opposite the 25° angle, correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.explanation: sin 25° = x/14, so x = 14 × sin 25° ≈ 5.92 cm. 33.13 cm comes from doing the opposite operation (x is on top).
steps: Label from the 25° angle: 14 cm is the hypotenuse; x is the opposite.
Hypotenuse and opposite means SOH: sin 25° = x/14.

mistakes.B: Step 3: x is on top in the equation, so multiply — you did the opposite.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you used cos. With the hypotenuse and the opposite, the ratio is sin (SOH).
mistakes.D: Step 2: you used tan. With the hypotenuse and the opposite, the ratio is sin (SOH).

questions.diagram_alt: A right-angled triangle with hypotenuse 14 cm, a 25° angle and the opposite side x.

questions.prompt: Find θ, correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: tan θ = 12/10, so θ = tan⁻¹(12/10) ≈ 50.2°. 39.8° is the other acute angle, which you get from the wrong ratio or the fraction upside down.
steps: Label from θ: 12 is the opposite and 10 is the adjacent.

mistakes.A: Step 2: tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent = 12/10. You used 10/12, which gives the other angle.
mistakes.B: Step 1: 12 is not the hypotenuse — it touches the right angle. Use tan with the two shorter sides.
mistakes.D: Step 2: cos needs the hypotenuse, which isn’t given. Use tan θ = 12/10.

questions.diagram_alt: A right-angled triangle with 10 m next to θ and 12 m across from θ.

questions.prompt: Find the length of the shorter side x.
questions.explanation: x² = 15² − 9² = 144, so x = √144 = 12 m. Adding the squares would make x longer than the hypotenuse.
steps: 15 m is the hypotenuse, so x² = 15² − 9².

mistakes.B: Step 1: 15 m is the hypotenuse, so subtract the squares — don’t add them.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you subtracted the lengths. Square them first.
mistakes.D: Step 3: 144 is x². Take the square root.

questions.diagram_alt: A right-angled triangle with hypotenuse 15 m, one shorter side 9 m and the other shorter side x.

questions.prompt: A box is 12 cm long, 9 cm wide and 8 cm high. Find the length d of its space diagonal.
questions.explanation: d² = 12² + 9² + 8² = 144 + 81 + 64 = 289, so d = 17 cm. 15 cm is only the base diagonal.

mistakes.A: Step 2: you added the lengths 12 + 9 + 8. Square each one, add, then square root.
mistakes.B: Step 1: 15 cm is only the diagonal across the base. Go up the 8 cm height as well.
mistakes.D: Step 3: 289 is d². Take the square root.

questions.diagram_alt: A box 12 cm long, 9 cm wide and 8 cm high, with the base diagonal dashed and the space diagonal d marked.

questions.prompt: Find the hypotenuse x, correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.explanation: cos 58° = 7/x, so x = 7 ÷ cos 58° ≈ 13.21 m. 3.71 m comes from doing the opposite operation (x is on the bottom).
steps: Label from the 58° angle: 7 m is the adjacent; x is the hypotenuse.
Adjacent and hypotenuse means CAH: cos 58° = 7/x.

mistakes.A: Step 3: x is on the bottom in the equation, so divide — you did the opposite.
mistakes.B: Step 2: you used sin. With the adjacent and the hypotenuse, the ratio is cos (CAH).
mistakes.C: Step 2: you used tan. With the adjacent and the hypotenuse, the ratio is cos (CAH).

questions.diagram_alt: A right-angled triangle with a 58° angle, the adjacent side 7 m and the hypotenuse x.

questions.prompt: Find θ, the angle between the 6 cm side and the 11 cm side, correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: cos θ = 6/11, so θ = cos⁻¹(6/11) ≈ 56.9°. 33.1° is the other acute angle, which you get from the wrong ratio or the fraction upside down.
steps: Label from θ: 6 is the adjacent and 11 is the hypotenuse.

mistakes.A: Step 2: the 6 side is the adjacent, so use cos, not sin. Your answer is the other acute angle.
mistakes.C: Step 2: 11 is the hypotenuse. Tan doesn’t use the hypotenuse — use cos.
mistakes.D: Step 2: tan needs two shorter sides, but 11 is the hypotenuse. Use cos θ = 6/11.

questions.diagram_alt: A right-angled triangle with 6 cm next to θ and hypotenuse 11 cm.

questions.prompt: You stand 45 m from the base of a building. The angle of elevation to its top is 33°. How tall is the building, to 1 decimal place?
questions.explanation: tan 33° = x/45, so x = 45 × tan 33° ≈ 29.2 m. 69.3 m comes from doing the opposite operation (x is on top).
steps: Label from the 33° angle: 45 m is the adjacent; x is the opposite.
Adjacent and opposite means TOA: tan 33° = x/45.

mistakes.B: Step 3: x is on top in the equation, so multiply — you did the opposite.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you used sin. With the adjacent and the opposite, the ratio is tan (TOA).
mistakes.D: Step 2: you used cos. With the adjacent and the opposite, the ratio is tan (TOA).

questions.diagram_alt: You stand 45 m from a building and look up at a 33° angle of elevation; the height is x.

questions.prompt: A cone has a slant height of 15 cm and a base radius of 9 cm. Find its vertical height h.
questions.explanation: h² = 15² − 9² = 225 − 81 = 144, so h = 12 cm. Adding the squares would make h longer than the slant side.
steps: The slant height (15 cm) is the hypotenuse; the radius and the height are the shorter sides.

mistakes.A: Step 2: the slant height is the hypotenuse, so subtract: 15² − 9², don’t add.
mistakes.B: Step 2: you subtracted the lengths 15 − 9. Square them first.
mistakes.C: Step 3: 144 is h². Take the square root.

questions.diagram_alt: A cone with radius 9 cm, slant height 15 cm and vertical height h.

questions.prompt: A 3.6 m ladder leans against a wall, making a 65° angle with the ground. How far is the foot of the ladder from the wall, to 2 decimal places?
questions.explanation: cos 65° = x/3.6, so x = 3.6 × cos 65° ≈ 1.52 m. 8.52 m comes from doing the opposite operation (x is on top).
steps: Label from the 65° angle: 3.6 m is the hypotenuse; x is the adjacent.
Hypotenuse and adjacent means CAH: cos 65° = x/3.6.

mistakes.A: Step 3: x is on top in the equation, so multiply — you did the opposite.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you used sin. With the hypotenuse and the adjacent, the ratio is cos (CAH).
mistakes.D: Step 2: you used tan. With the hypotenuse and the adjacent, the ratio is cos (CAH).

questions.diagram_alt: A 3.6 m ladder leaning against a wall at 65° to the ground; the distance x from the foot of the ladder to the wall is marked.

questions.prompt: From the top of a 120 m cliff, the angle of depression to a yacht is 18°. How far is the yacht from the base of the cliff, to 1 decimal place?
questions.explanation: tan 18° = 120/x, so x = 120 ÷ tan 18° ≈ 369.3 m. 39.0 m comes from doing the opposite operation (x is on the bottom).
steps: Label from the 18° angle: 120 m is the opposite; x is the adjacent.
Opposite and adjacent means TOA: tan 18° = 120/x.

mistakes.A: Step 3: x is on the bottom in the equation, so divide — you did the opposite.
mistakes.B: Step 2: you used sin. With the opposite and the adjacent, the ratio is tan (TOA).
mistakes.D: Step 2: you used cos. With the opposite and the adjacent, the ratio is tan (TOA).

questions.diagram_alt: A 120 m cliff with an 18° angle of depression from its top to a yacht; the distance x along the water is marked.

questions.prompt: Use a calculator to find cos 72°, correct to 4 decimal places.
questions.explanation: In degree mode, cos 72° ≈ 0.3090. −0.9673 is what radians mode gives.
steps: Check the calculator shows D or DEG (degree mode).

mistakes.B: Step 2: that is sin 72°. Press the cos key.
mistakes.C: Step 2: that is tan 72°. Press the cos key.
mistakes.D: Step 1: your calculator is in radians mode. Switch to degrees (D or DEG on the screen).

questions.prompt: A 2.5 m pole must fit completely inside a crate 1.6 m long, 1.2 m wide and 1.5 m high. Will it fit?

options.A: No — the base diagonal is only 2 m
options.B: No — the longest edge is only 1.6 m
options.C: Yes — the space diagonal is exactly 2.5 m

questions.explanation: The space diagonal is √(1.6² + 1.2² + 1.5²) = √6.25 = 2.5 m, so the pole fits exactly (just!). The base diagonal (2 m) is too short, but the pole can tilt.
steps: The longest straight line inside a box is the space diagonal.
d = √6.25 = 2.5 m — exactly the pole’s length, so it fits.

mistakes.A: Step 1: the pole can tilt up through the box. Use the space diagonal, not the base diagonal.
mistakes.B: Step 1: the longest straight line inside a box is the space diagonal, not an edge.
mistakes.D: Step 2: a straight pole can’t bend along three edges. Square, add, then square root.

questions.diagram_alt: A crate 1.6 m long, 1.2 m wide and 1.5 m high with its base diagonal dashed and the space diagonal d marked.

questions.prompt: Lily holds a kite string 1.2 m above the ground. The string is 60 m long, straight, and makes an angle of elevation of 50°. How high is the kite above the ground, to 1 decimal place?
questions.explanation: Above her hand: 60 × sin 50° ≈ 45.96 m. Add the 1.2 m: about 47.2 m. 46.0 m forgets the height of her hand.
steps: The string is the hypotenuse (60 m); the height above her hand is opposite the 50° angle: sin 50° = x/60.

mistakes.A: Step 3: that is only the height above Lily’s hand. Add the 1.2 m.
mistakes.C: Step 1: the height is opposite the 50° angle, so use sin, not cos.
mistakes.D: Step 1: the string (60 m) is the hypotenuse, so use sin, not tan.

questions.diagram_alt: Lily’s hand 1.2 m above the ground holding a straight 60 m kite string at a 50° angle of elevation to the kite.
